beliefs: The box reverses the order of characters in the input string [E1]
All Unicode whitespace characters are removed from the output rather than preserved [E2, E5, E8]
Reversal happens first, then whitespace is stripped from the reversed result [E2, E4, E15, E24]
Case, digits, symbols, and non-whitespace invisible/format characters (ZWJ, ZWNJ, BOM, soft hyphen, word joiner) are preserved as-is, only order changes and whitespace is dropped [E1, E9]
Reversal is by Unicode code point: a valid surrogate pair is treated as one unit and stays intact [E6, E7, E16, E17, E23]
Lone surrogates and unpaired UTF-16 code units are reversed as individual code points without error or alteration [E11, E12]
A surrogate pair split by whitespace is NOT recombined: reversal happens first, so the halves stay separate and whitespace is then dropped [E13, E14, E18, E19, E24]
Whitespace between a lone high and lone low surrogate is removed but the halves are never merged into an astral character [E18, E19, E24]
Because reversal is by code point, adjacent valid surrogate pairs are grouped as units and stay intact [E6, E7, E16, E17, E23]
notes: Reverted to code-point reversal (grouping valid surrogate pairs) since E6/E7/E16/E17 require it; E23's apparent code-unit behavior is explained by lone surrogates not pairing. Split pairs stay separate because reversal precedes whitespace stripping (E24).
